comment: The governance principle correctly prioritises data quality, but it may imply that minimum data-quality thresholds can be defined universally before a component becomes operational. Fitness for purpose differs by use case and risk.

anchor.note: p.31-32 l.Lines 194-223 read as the printed page; section 2.3 agrees

public.text: The governance principle correctly prioritises data quality, but it may imply that minimum data-quality thresholds can be defined universally before a component becomes operational. Fitness for purpose differs by use case and risk.
public.suggestedRevision: Require use-case-specific data-quality criteria, including completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency, provenance, and acceptable error thresholds, with stricter levels for safety-critical use cases.
